title: xAI Launches Grok Bot, an AI 'Teammate' That Works Your Apps Around the Clock
excerpt: Grok Bot gets its own cloud computer, signs into your tools, and runs tasks in parallel — marking xAI's push from chatbot to autonomous agent.
body:
• xAI launched Grok Bot, an autonomous AI agent that operates as a virtual teammate with its own persistent cloud computer.
  • Bots can sign into users' apps and websites, learn workflows by watching them performed once, and run tasks 24/7 — even when the user's device is off.
  • Multiple bots can work in parallel and hand off tasks to each other in shared threads.
  • Available now for Cursor Ultra ($200/month) and SuperGrok Heavy subscribers on macOS, Windows and iOS.

Elon Musk's xAI has launched Grok Bot, a new AI agent platform that moves beyond the chatbot paradigm into autonomous task execution. Instead of answering questions in a conversation window, Grok Bot operates as an AI "teammate" that owns a persistent cloud computer, signs into users' tools, and works through assignments around the clock.

The product, announced this week, represents xAI's most significant push into the AI agent market, where it competes with offerings from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google.

How It Works

Each Grok Bot instance gets its own persistent cloud computer — a virtual machine that stays running even when the user's laptop is closed. Users can log the bot into their existing apps and websites, from CRM platforms like Zendesk to email and spreadsheet tools, and it uses them the same way a human colleague would.

The most notable feature is workflow learning. Users can ask a bot to watch as they complete a task once. The bot saves the sequence as a "routine" and runs it independently from that point forward. Combined with scheduled execution, this turns Grok Bot into an always-on worker that can handle recurring tasks without further prompting.

Multi-Agent Collaboration

xAI designed Grok Bot for multi-agent workflows. Users can create multiple bots, each assigned to a different domain — one on sales pipeline, another on customer support, a third on internal reporting. The bots work in parallel and, when placed in the same thread, can pass work between themselves.

This architecture moves the product beyond single-shot AI assistance into something closer to a small team of digital workers. It reflects a broader industry trend toward "agentic AI" that can plan, execute, and iterate on multi-step tasks without human intervention at each stage.

"The biggest advantage is each one owns its own routines, context, and domain."

— Hacker News commenter on Grok Bot launch

Pricing and Access

Grok Bot is available to Cursor Ultra subscribers at $200 per month and Cursor Premium Teams users at $120 per seat per month. SuperGrok Heavy subscribers also get access. Enterprise availability is expected in the coming weeks.

Each subscription includes a weekly token usage allocation, with additional usage billed based on token cost. All bots within a user's account share a single persistent cloud computer — isolated per user, not per bot — meaning bots can access the same files, browser sessions and login states.

Security and Privacy Concerns

The launch has sparked debate about the security implications of giving AI agents persistent access to authenticated apps. Users on Hacker News raised concerns about prompt injection risks and the trustworthiness of storing session tokens with xAI.

xAI says Grok Bot uses the same SSO, authentication and privacy-mode infrastructure as Cursor, with encryption in transit and at rest and a training opt-out option. Sensitive actions can be routed through an "Auto Review" gate before execution, and enterprise admins can set DLP policies, certificates and network controls.

The Bigger Picture

Grok Bot enters a rapidly crowding field. Anthropic's Claude has computer-use capabilities, OpenAI's Codex operates as a coding agent, and Google's Project Mariner targets browser-based tasks. What distinguishes xAI's approach is the persistent virtual machine model — giving each user a dedicated cloud computer their bots inhabit permanently rather than spinning up fresh sessions for each interaction.

The product is available on macOS, Windows and iOS, with the desktop and mobile apps serving as the primary interface for managing bots and reviewing their work.
